transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, I... I came in because my husband, he's the one who practically dragged me here, actually. He and the people at the warehouse where I work, they all keep acting like I'm crazy or something. Like I'm making things up. But I'm not. I've been working the freight line for four years now, and I know how things run, okay? I know the system. And lately, I know they have been watching my moves. Like, really watching me. I can feel it when I'm on the floor, moving the stock. And it's not just that they're watching me, they are actively messing with my work. They've been changing the pallet counts on my shifts. I count them, I log them, and then suddenly the numbers are different. And I know exactly why they're doing it. It's because of that supervisor spot that opened up last month. They know I'm the hardest worker there, and they are doing everything they can to make me look bad, to make me look like I can't keep track of the inventory, just to keep me from getting that promotion. My husband says I'm just stressed and not sleeping, but he doesn't see what goes on at that warehouse. He doesn't see how they look at me when I walk past the breakroom.
Have you ever heard any voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?

Well... it's funny you ask that, because, you know, the warehouse is loud. It's just so loud with the forklifts always backing up with that beep-beep-beep, and the belts running, and people yelling over the machinery. So usually, if you hear something, you just think it's the noise, right? But... well, lately, and this is another thing my husband just absolutely refuses to understand, I'll be way down in one of the back aisles—like aisle seven, where we keep the seasonal overstock, so it's usually dead quiet back there—and I'll be doing my counts, and I swear to you, Dr. Smith, I hear this man. 

It's a man's voice, deep, like he's standing right behind my shoulder. And he says, clear as day, he says, "Nicole, check it again." Just like that. "Nicole, check it again." And I whip around, because I immediately think it's one of the guys from the loading dock trying to sneak up on me or mess with my numbers, like I was telling you about before, but there is absolutely nobody there. I look up and down the whole aisle, and it's empty. 

And the thing is, it's not just at work, either, which is what really gets me. I'll be at home, right in my own house, just minding my own business folding clothes. I'll be folding my husband's work shirts or matching up socks on the couch, the TV isn't even on, just totally quiet, and there it is again. "Nicole, check it again." Right in my ear. My husband will be all the way out in the garage, nobody else is even in the room or anywhere near me, but the voice is just as real as you talking to me right now. I keep telling him, how can I be making that up if I hear it that clearly?

Aside from these experiences, have you noticed any significant changes in your mood, such as periods where you feel extremely low and hopeless, or perhaps periods where you feel unusually energetic or like you don't need sleep?

Energetic? I mean... yeah, I guess you could say that. Some days I wake up and I just feel completely fired up, like my blood is buzzing and absolutely nobody can slow me down. I'll go into the warehouse and I'm clearing pallets twice as fast as the guys, and then I'll come home and I don't even want to sit down. I'm just going and going, cleaning things, organizing everything. I feel like I could run the whole world on those days. 

But the problem is... well, it's my husband again. He just doesn't get it when I'm in that zone. I'll be getting so much done, finally feeling good and productive, and he'll come up to me and ask just one small question. Like, something completely mundane about the kids' school drop-off, or he'll ask about my work schedule for the rest of the week. Just poking his nose in. And I just... I completely snap at him. I mean, I go off. It just makes me so incredibly mad because it feels exactly like he's trying to control me, you know? 

Like he's trying to micromanage what I'm doing or interrupt my flow when I finally have the energy to get my life sorted out. He says I get vicious and that my mood flips out of nowhere, but if he would just leave me alone and stop interrogating me about my schedule or the kids when I'm clearly busy, we wouldn't even have a problem. I'm just trying to get things done, and he's always standing there asking these little questions, trying to put a leash on me or something. It just makes my skin crawl when he tries to box me in like that.

When you have these periods where you feel 'fired up' and get very angry, do they happen at the same time as the thoughts about people watching you and the voice you hear, or do you sometimes have those high-energy, irritable moods when you aren't feeling paranoid or hearing that voice?

Well, see, it's all kind of tangled up together, honestly. I mean... if I really think about it, like, take a couple of weeks ago for example. I was barely sleeping at all. Maybe two, three hours a night, tops, and I didn't even feel tired. I was just pushing and pushing, taking on all these extra shifts at the warehouse because, like I told you, I'm trying to prove I'm the one who deserves that supervisor spot. And it wasn't just work, either. I had so much energy I started doing boxing, just hitting the heavy bag for hours because my blood was just humming, you know? And then on top of that, I was doing all this extra work down at the church, organizing the whole food pantry, sorting all the donations, making sure every single can was faced perfectly because nobody else was doing it right. 

And right in the middle of all that—during those exact same weeks where I'm going a hundred miles an hour with the extra shifts and the boxing and the church work—that's exactly when all the other stuff was happening, too. That's when I was hearing that man's voice the absolute most. I'd be flying through a pallet, totally fired up, and right in my ear, there it is. And that was the exact same time I was absolutely, one hundred percent sure that the people at the warehouse were setting me up. I'd be working circles around them on my extra shifts, and I just knew they were watching me, messing with my logs to make me look incompetent so I wouldn't get the promotion. 

So, yeah, to answer your question, it's all at the same time. It's not like I have the energy one week and then the voice the next week or whatever. It's all happening right on top of each other, which is exactly why it makes me so incredibly mad when my husband tries to interrupt me or slow me down. I'm dealing with all these people at work actively trying to sabotage me, and I'm hearing this guy telling me to check my numbers, and I'm just trying to power through and get everything done at the warehouse and the church, and my husband just wants to stand there and nag me about the kids' schedule. It's just... it's all happening at once, you know?

Have you ever had these experiences of hearing voices or feeling like people were watching you during times when you were feeling completely normal or low, rather than when you were feeling that high-energy, 'fired up' way?

Well... yeah, actually. Now that you bring it up, it's not just when I'm going a hundred miles an hour. Because... I mean, if I really think back to maybe a month or two ago, I actually had a really quiet few weeks. Things had settled down a lot. I wasn't racing around the house organizing every little thing, and I was actually sleeping closer to normal. I was getting like six or seven hours, waking up feeling just regular, you know? Not buzzing, not exhausted, just... going in for my regular shifts, coming home, sitting on the couch. A totally normal routine. My husband was actually off my back for a minute because I wasn't snapping at him and I wasn't taking all those extra hours at the warehouse. 

But the thing is... even during that quiet time, even when my blood wasn't humming and I was totally calm... the rest of it absolutely did not stop. I'd be walking down the aisle, completely relaxed, just doing my regular job, and I still heard that exact same man's voice telling me to check things. Just out of nowhere, clear as a bell. And I still knew, without a shadow of a doubt, that those guys were changing the pallet counts against me. I would count a pallet, log it perfectly, and I just knew they were going into the system and altering the numbers to make me look bad. 

So it didn't even matter that I was sleeping fine and feeling totally normal. I was still hearing the voice, and I still fully believed they were sabotaging my pallet counts. Which is exactly why I keep trying to tell my husband that it's not just me being stressed out or whatever he wants to call it! I'll be perfectly fine, having a completely normal week, and I still hear it, and they're still messing with my work. It just never really stops, no matter how much sleep I get.
